name: Audible verb endings
instruction: A plural subject where the verb form actually changes sound.

name: Noun gender
instruction: A noun taking an adjective, so the gender is visible.

name: pas de after negation
instruction: Negating a sentence with an indefinite object.
examples: Il ne mange pas de viande

name: Partitive articles
instruction: Some quantity of an uncountable thing.

name: The article on a generic noun
instruction: Liking or hating something in general, where English uses no article.

name: au, du, aux, des
instruction: Going to or coming from a place whose name takes le or les.

name: il y a
instruction: Saying something is there.
examples: Il y a une pharmacie en face

name: c'est against il est
instruction: Identifying somebody against describing what they do.

name: Possessives agree with the thing owned
instruction: Somebody else's possession, where English marks the owner's sex instead.

name: Where the adjective goes
instruction: A description whose adjective English puts in front.

name: aller plus infinitive
instruction: Something about to happen, or planned for today.

name: Questions by intonation alone
instruction: A casual yes-no question between friends.

name: est-ce que
instruction: A neutral question, spoken or written, without inverting.

name: on for nous
instruction: What you and the people with you are doing.

name: ne…pas around the verb
instruction: A plain denial, with the negation wrapped round the conjugated verb.

name: à, en, au before place names
instruction: Being in or going to a city or country.

name: The imperative
instruction: Telling somebody to do something, and telling them not to.

name: Reflexive verbs
instruction: A daily routine, where English needs no pronoun at all.
examples: Je me lève à sept heures

name: de after a quantity word
instruction: How much of something there is.

name: Fixed politeness
instruction: Asking a stranger for something in a shop or on the street.

name: je voudrais, j'aimerais
instruction: Ordering or requesting, in the fixed polite forms only.

name: tu against vous
instruction: Addressing somebody the learner has just met, or somebody older.

name: States with avoir
instruction: Being hungry, cold, afraid, right, or a certain age.

name: être or avoir in the passé composé
instruction: A movement or reflexive verb in the past.

name: Object pronouns before the verb
instruction: Replacing a stated object — English speakers repeat the noun instead.

name: Verbs with à or de
instruction: penser à against penser de, commencer à, essayer de.

name: Liaison
instruction: Obligatory liaison across a determiner or pronoun boundary.

name: Silent written agreement
instruction: Plural -s and participle agreement that cannot be heard.

name: The imparfait
instruction: How things used to be, or what was going on at the time.
examples: Quand j'étais petit, j'habitais à Lyon

name: The futur simple
instruction: A plan or a prediction further off than tonight.

name: venir de
instruction: Something finished moments ago.

name: être en train de
instruction: Insisting an action is under way right now.
examples: Je suis en train de travailler

name: depuis with the present
instruction: How long something has been going on and still is.

name: il y a, pendant, dans, depuis
instruction: How long ago, for how long, and in how long.

name: plus, moins, aussi … que
instruction: Setting two things side by side.
examples: Il est plus grand que moi

name: The superlative
instruction: The best or the worst of a group, with the adjective in its own slot.
examples: le film le plus long de l'année

name: meilleur against mieux
instruction: Saying something is better, where English has one word for both.

name: Pronouns with the imperative
instruction: Telling somebody to do it, then telling them not to.

name: Question words at the end
instruction: A casual question with où, quand, comment or combien left in place.

name: Adverbs in -ment
instruction: How something was done, with the adverb in its French slot in a compound tense.

name: si with the present
instruction: A real condition and what will follow from it.
examples: Si tu viens, on ira au cinéma

name: il faut plus infinitive
instruction: A general obligation with nobody in particular responsible.

name: qui, que, où
instruction: Joining two statements about the same person or thing.

name: moi, toi, lui, eux
instruction: Emphasising who, or naming somebody after a preposition.

name: Negating an infinitive
instruction: Telling somebody not to do something, with both negation words together in front.
examples: Il m'a dit de ne pas venir

name: se for each other
instruction: Two people doing something to one another.
examples: Ils se sont rencontrés à Paris

name: Possession with de
instruction: Whose something is.

name: jouer à against jouer de
instruction: Playing a sport, and playing an instrument.

name: savoir against connaître
instruction: Knowing a fact or a skill against knowing a person or a place.

name: faire du, de la
instruction: A sport, an instrument or a chore taken up as an activity.

name: avoir besoin de, avoir envie de
instruction: Needing something, or feeling like doing something.

name: ne…que, plus, jamais, personne
instruction: Negation other than pas.

name: y and en
instruction: Replacing a place or a quantity. No English equivalent, so never reached for.

name: Passé composé against imparfait
instruction: A narrative with both a background and an event.
examples: Je regardais la télé quand il est arrivé

name: The subjunctive
instruction: After il faut que and vouloir que — learners restructure to dodge it.

name: The plus-que-parfait
instruction: Something already over before another past event.
examples: Il était déjà parti quand je suis arrivé

name: si with the imparfait
instruction: An unreal present condition and what would follow.
examples: Si j'avais le temps, je viendrais

name: The conditional to soften
instruction: Advice or a suggestion pitched short of an order.

name: The future after quand
instruction: Something to do once another future thing happens, where English keeps the present.
examples: Dès qu'il sera prêt, on partira

name: The gérondif
instruction: Two things at once, or how something was done.

name: The passive
instruction: An action whose agent does not matter.
examples: La maison a été construite en 1920

name: on instead of a passive
instruction: Where English says something is done, with nobody named.
examples: On m'a dit que c'était fermé

name: que cannot be dropped
instruction: Reporting what somebody said or thinks, where English can leave out 'that'.

name: si, ce que, ce qui in reported questions
instruction: Reporting a question instead of asking it.

name: où for a moment in time
instruction: The day, the year or the moment something happened.
examples: le jour où je l'ai rencontrée

name: celui, celle, ceux
instruction: The one belonging to somebody, or the one that does something.

name: quelqu'un, chacun, certains, plusieurs
instruction: Unnamed people or things, in numbers left vague.

name: tout, tous, toute, toutes
instruction: All of something, everyone, or something done entirely.

name: parce que, car, puisque, comme
instruction: A reason the listener already knows, against one they do not.
examples: Comme il pleuvait, on est restés

name: du coup
instruction: A consequence, in conversation.
examples: Du coup, j'ai raté le train
Il était fermé, du coup on est rentrés

name: c'est … qui, c'est … que
instruction: Insisting it was this one and not another.

name: avant de plus infinitive
instruction: One thing before another, the same person doing both.
examples: Avant de partir, ferme la fenêtre

name: pour que
instruction: Doing something so that somebody else can do something.
examples: Je te le dis pour que tu sois prêt

name: The subjunctive after feeling
instruction: Being glad, sorry or afraid about what somebody else does.
examples: Je suis content que tu sois là

name: il est difficile de
instruction: Judging an action in general, with the action pushed after the adjective.

name: manquer and plaire flip the subject
instruction: Missing somebody, or liking something, where French swaps who does what.

name: Two pronouns together
instruction: me le, le lui — avoided even by learners comfortable with one.

name: The relative dont
instruction: A relative clause whose verb takes de.

name: The subjunctive after doubt
instruction: Doubting or denying that something is the case.
examples: Je ne pense pas qu'il ait raison

name: bien que, quoique
instruction: Conceding a point that cuts against what you are about to say.
examples: Bien qu'il soit tard, je continue
Quoiqu'elle ait tort, je la comprends

name: avant que, jusqu'à ce que, sans que
instruction: A conjunction leaving the second clause unrealised: before, until, without, provided that.

name: lequel, auquel, duquel
instruction: A relative clause whose verb needs a preposition other than de.
examples: la raison pour laquelle je suis venu

name: Ce qui …, c'est …
instruction: Naming what bothers or pleases you, then saying what it is.
examples: Ce qui m'énerve, c'est le bruit
Ce que je veux, c'est du calme

name: The futur antérieur
instruction: Something already finished by a point still to come.
examples: Quand tu arriveras, il sera parti

name: The conditionnel passé
instruction: Regretting how something turned out, or what was not done.
examples: Si j'avais su, je ne serais pas venu
Tu aurais dû me le dire

name: Reported speech in the past
instruction: Reporting what somebody said, from a past vantage point.
examples: Elle m'a demandé si j'avais fini

name: après avoir, après être
instruction: One thing after another is finished, the same person doing both.
examples: Après avoir mangé, il est sorti
Après être rentrée, elle a appelé

name: The participe présent
instruction: A written clause giving the reason or the circumstance, replacing a because-clause.
examples: Ne sachant pas quoi faire, il a attendu

name: Questions with a bare infinitive
instruction: Wondering aloud what to do, with nobody as subject.

name: Inversion in questions
instruction: A formal written question, or an interview.

name: Keeping ne in writing
instruction: Negation in formal writing, where dropping ne would be wrong.
examples: Il ne s'agit pas d'une erreur
Nous ne pouvons accepter cette offre

name: nous in formal register
instruction: A written report or a formal address, where on would be too casual.
examples: Nous vous prions de nous excuser

name: avoir beau
instruction: However much somebody tries, nothing changes.
examples: Il a beau insister, je refuse
J'ai beau chercher, je ne trouve rien

name: il s'agit de
instruction: What a text or a situation is about, with no personal subject.
examples: Il ne s'agit pas de ça

name: faire faire, se faire
instruction: Having somebody else do something for you, or having something done to you.
examples: Il s'est fait voler son vélo

name: cependant, toutefois, en revanche
instruction: Setting one fact against another inside an argument.
examples: C'est cher ; en revanche, la qualité est là

name: plus … plus …
instruction: The more one thing happens, the more another does.
examples: Plus j'y pense, moins je comprends

name: Adjectives followed by à or de
instruction: An adjective with an action hanging off it.
examples: Je suis content de te voir

name: en against de lui
instruction: Replacing a de-phrase, where it matters whether it stands for a person.

name: The passé simple
instruction: Written narrative only — correctly absent from speech.

name: The past subjunctive
instruction: Judging or regretting something already done.
examples: Je regrette qu'il soit parti si tôt

name: The subjunctive after a superlative
instruction: The only one, the first one, or the best one that does something.
examples: C'est le seul film qui m'ait plu
la meilleure chose qui puisse arriver

name: The subjunctive in a relative clause
instruction: Looking for something that may not exist.
examples: Je cherche quelqu'un qui sache le russe
Il n'y a rien qui vaille la peine

name: The expletive ne
instruction: Formal writing after fearing, unless, or before, where the ne denies nothing.
examples: Je crains qu'il ne soit trop tard
à moins qu'il ne change d'avis

name: Inversion after a fronted adverb
instruction: Opening on perhaps, thus, or hardly, in formal prose.
examples: À peine était-il sorti que le téléphone a sonné

name: or, ainsi, néanmoins, dès lors
instruction: Turning an argument on a fact the reader has not weighed.
examples: Or, rien ne prouve le contraire

name: quitte à
instruction: Accepting a cost in order to go ahead anyway.
examples: Je le dirai, quitte à le vexer

name: sans pour autant
instruction: Granting one thing while refusing the next.
examples: Il a accepté, sans pour autant approuver

name: Nominalisation
instruction: A headline or a report where the action becomes a noun.
examples: L'annulation du vol a été confirmée

name: The impersonal passive
instruction: An official announcement with nobody named as author.
examples: Il a été décidé de reporter la réunion
Il est prévu que les travaux durent un an

name: The conditional for unverified claims
instruction: Reporting something the press has not confirmed.
examples: Le suspect aurait quitté le pays
Le bilan s'élèverait à trois blessés

name: au cas où, à supposer que
instruction: A precaution against something that may well not happen.
examples: Au cas où il pleuvrait, prends un parapluie
à supposer que ce soit vrai

name: quel que soit, quoi que, où que
instruction: Whatever, wherever, however much — none of it changes the outcome.

name: ayant, étant plus participle
instruction: A written clause saying what had already been done.
examples: Ayant terminé son travail, il est sorti
Étant arrivés en retard, ils ont attendu

name: duquel where dont is impossible
instruction: A relative whose de sits inside a prepositional phrase.
examples: le village près duquel nous vivons
la loi au nom de laquelle il agit

name: Referring back with a noun
instruction: Resuming what you just argued without repeating the words.

name: faire l'objet de, procéder à
instruction: A formal report where the verb carries none of the meaning.
examples: Le dossier fera l'objet d'un examen
Il a procédé à une vérification

name: Participle agreement with reflexives
instruction: A reflexive verb in the past that also has its own direct object.

name: Si …, c'est que …
instruction: Framing what an argument really turns on.
examples: Si je le dis, c'est que c'est vrai
Ce dont il s'agit, c'est de la méthode

name: ne faire que
instruction: Somebody who does nothing but the one thing.
examples: Il ne fait que se plaindre
Je n'ai fait que suivre les consignes

name: Formal verb choice
instruction: A report where the everyday verb would read as too plain.

name: The imperfect subjunctive
instruction: A literary past narrative pulling the subordinate verb back with it.

name: The passé antérieur
instruction: A literary narrative where one action closes just before the next opens.
examples: Dès qu'il eut fini, il sortit
Quand elle fut partie, le silence retomba

name: soi
instruction: A general statement about anyone, pointing back at that anyone.

name: Verbal adjective against participle
instruction: A written -ant form used to describe rather than to act.

name: Compound nouns in the plural
instruction: Several of a compound noun, written out.

name: Agreements that go against the pattern
instruction: A written quantity, a half, or a document attached.

name: Understatement
instruction: Praising or condemning by denying the opposite.

name: il n'en demeure pas moins que
instruction: Conceding a point in formal argument and overriding it in the same breath.
examples: Il n'en demeure pas moins que le problème persiste

name: que resuming a conjunction
instruction: A second subordinate clause hanging off the same conjunction.
examples: Bien qu'il soit tard et que je sois fatigué, je reste
Si tu viens et que tu as le temps

name: Inverted subject in a relative clause
instruction: A long written relative whose subject follows its verb.
examples: les mesures qu'a prises le gouvernement
le jour où mourut son père

name: de sorte que with either mood
instruction: A conjunction meaning a result with the indicative and an aim with the subjunctive.

name: Fronting the adjective
instruction: An essay opening on the judgement rather than the subject.
examples: Rares sont ceux qui y parviennent

name: il importe que, il en va de même
instruction: A formal statement of what matters, with no personal subject.
examples: Il importe que chacun soit informé
Il en va de même pour les autres

name: non sans
instruction: Admitting something came off, but not easily.
examples: Il a réussi, non sans peine

name: pour peu que, si tant est que
instruction: A remote written condition, granted only for argument's sake.
examples: Pour peu qu'il pleuve, tout est annulé
si tant est que ce soit vrai

name: cela étant, en l'occurrence
instruction: Qualifying your own point mid-conversation, in articulate speech.
examples: Cela étant, je comprends votre position
En l'occurrence, ce n'est pas le cas
